messages:
Alex: Quick handoff — FYI on noisy nvme_iops_spike and prefix-cache-evictions alerts. No customer impact, started after k8s nodepool tweak earlier. Leaving mitigation steps and watchlist.

oncall-bot: [ALERT] nvme_iops_spike firing (3/5) in prod-us-east-1 — runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/NVME_NOISE

Marta: Got it. How long do you expect noise to continue? Do we mute or change thresholds?

Alex: Probably a few hours while autoscaler stabilizes. I muted nvme alert for 30m as a trial. Command I ran:
```
curl -X POST "https://ops-api.local/alerts/mute" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"alert":"nvme_iops_spike","until":"2026-03-17T03:00:00Z","reason":"post-rollout noise"}'
```
Also added a temporary rule for prefix-cache-evictions to require 3 consecutive firing windows.

Ryan: Suggest we change alert to `count_over_time() >= 3` for 5m window instead of immediate. Query we use in grafana:
```
sum by(node) (increase(prefix_cache_evicts_total[5m])) > 5
```
I'll open a quick PR to adjust the expression and link it here.

Samir: Please add this thread to tonight's rotation notes — I'll cover 22:00–02:00 if it persists.

Marta: Thanks Alex — can you add the list of affected nodepools? I'll hand off to infra if it doesn't cool off by 00:00.

Alex: Affected: nodepool-gpu-1, nodepool-gpu-2 (us-east), maybe one host in us-west. PR: https://github.com/redwood/monitoring/pull/342

Jin: If the pattern keeps repeating after the PR, escalate to eng-infra and include kernel logs: `dmesg | grep nvme`.

oncall-bot: Note added to handoff: nvme noise — Samir covering 22:00–02:00. Reminder set for 21:50.

Marta: Ack. Adding to watchlist doc: https://redwood.internal/team/oncall/watchlist.md#nvme-noise

Alex: Leaving the oncall handoff — ping me here if it spikes again, otherwise I'll clear my muting when autoscaler settles. :+1:

Ryan: PR merged, will monitor for 30m and report back.

Samir: Watching, will post updates if anything changes.

Marta: Closing our side for now. Reopen thread if alerts resurface.
